returns.name: Quarterly wage report and premium payment (Employer e-Services)
contents: Premiums become due and payable quarterly on or before the last day of the month following the calendar quarter (rule 0800-10-01-.02(1)): April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31.
Wage reports are filed in Employer e-Services and the premium paid there afterwards; TNPAWS and TPU no longer take wage reports.
The taxable wage base is $7,000 for 2026 (the Department's table).

notModelled: The rule does not state a weekend or holiday roll, so the next business day is assumed.
The Department's support pages (lwdsupport.tn.gov) refuse automated access and were not read; the electronic filing mandate in T.C.A. 50-7-404 (Justia copy refused access) is not recorded.
The rate notice and the variable-wage-base rule: the base varies with the trust fund balance and is $7,000 for 2026.

channels.description: Tennessee Employer e-Services: wage reports, premium payments and delinquent quarters
enrollment: Register as a Tennessee employer for unemployment insurance and sign up for an account on Employer e-Services (https://jobs4tnui.tn.gov/employer/_/); the FAQ says TNPAWS credentials do not work there and new accounts are created by signing up for an online account.

notModelled: Tennessee has no wage income tax on wages, so there is no state withholding.

New-hire reporting (Tennessee): the days are counted from the hire date, as calendar days with no weekend roll; the directory's data elements, transmission methods and independent-contractor rule are in the federal matrix and were not transcribed.

newHire.form: New-hire report (federal Form W-4 or an equivalent) to the Tennessee State Directory of New Hires; within 20 days of hire date
